text: Legal entities and ledgers answer "who legally exists" and "what book records it." Neither actually processes a transaction. That job belongs to the business unit, which you'll touch constantly in every later course.

A business unit is an operational, transaction-processing organization that performs specific business functions — processing invoices, orders, requisitions. It's assigned to exactly one primary ledger, usually associated with one legal entity.

The relationship isn't strictly one-to-one. A single legal entity might contain several business units. A single business unit might even process transactions for more than one legal entity, acting as a shared service provider.

New consultants sometimes treat legal entity and business unit as the same thing. They're not. Legal entity is about statutory obligations; business unit is about how the company organizes its operational work.

Business units are also the lens that determines which company policies apply to a transaction, through reference data sets, covered in lesson twelve. Next up, lesson eleven: business unit functions and assignments.
